title: run-command reads a REPL error reply as a successful elaboration
description:
run-command computes :ok as (empty? errs) where errs comes from (:messages r). A reply carrying no :messages key therefore yields errs = [] and :ok = true.

That reply shape occurs. apply-tactic hit it 19 times in gen-27 alone: the REPL returns {:message ... :ok ...} — an error response — when it rejects a request. For apply-tactic this was fixed in vf-4tw, where absence of :goals had been read as 'no goals remain'. run-command has the same defect and was flagged in that issue but never checked.

The consequence is worse here. verify_lean branches on (:ok r); with :ok true and no sorries it runs the faithfulness judge and, on a pass, records a CONFIRMED artifact. So a REPL error can be laundered into a verified result — the same class that produced the three classical artifacts, via the other entry point.

Fix: require an affirmative signal, not merely the absence of a negative. A successful cmd reply carries :env; an error reply carries :message. Absence is not assent.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: :ok now requires an affirmative :env rather than the absence of error messages, and the REPL's rejection message reaches the caller.

title: lean_search is free, so branches search instead of proving
description:
lean_search is :neutral, so it neither counts against a branch nor advances it. A branch can therefore search indefinitely, and does.

gen-27 first 92 turns: 62 lean_search against 3 verify_lean, 5 proof_start, 2 proof_step. 79 of 92 turns neutral. Longest consecutive search runs with no verification attempt in between: B1 11, B2 13, B3 8.

The harness noticed and was ignored. progress-stalled fired 6 times, 0 met, 6 unmet. prologue-cap fired 11 times, 0 met, 11 unmet. Seventeen nudges, zero compliance.

That is the campaign's established finding restated: gates that WITHHOLD change behaviour, gates that SUGGEST do not (arbiter/prefill-for). Both of these only suggest, and the no-good-match message added in vf-f5c also only suggests — a branch reads 'Mathlib may not have this, prove it directly' and searches again with different words.

Withhold instead: after a run of consecutive searches with no verification attempt, refuse the search and say what clears it. :mechanics, since nothing was claimed and nothing tested. Any verification attempt resets the count, so a branch that alternates search and proof is never touched.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: eight consecutive searches without an engine attempt refuse the ninth, and any attempt clears the count including a failing one.

title: A branch whose Lean session dies is poisoned, then culled for it
description:
Two defects that compound.

1. lean-session! returns (:lean branch) without checking alive?, so once a session dies the branch is handed the corpse on every later call and can never obtain a working one. octave-session! is the same.

2. A REPL death that arrives as a RETURNED ERROR — {:error ...} from run-command — goes through fail and is charged :failure. The same outage arriving as a THROWN exception goes through unavailable and is :neutral. The returned-error path is the common one.

gen-26 B3: t28 a genuine Lean error, t30 'The Lean REPL failed: Lean REPL I/O failed', t32 'The Lean REPL session is dead'. Culled after 3 consecutive failures, two of which were infrastructure. It made no further Lean call because every one would have used the dead session.

unavailable's own docstring records the same incident two generations earlier: 'gen-18 B3 was culled after six consecutive failures... One of the six was Lean is unavailable, a fact about the process pool.' The fix was applied to the catch path and not to the returned-error path.

This is the vf-jki pattern again — an infrastructure fault charged to the counter that decides whether a branch lives — with the extra twist that the branch cannot recover even if the pool has healthy sessions.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: sessions are checked for liveness before reuse, and a dead REPL is neutral wherever it surfaces rather than only on the throw path. gen-27 is the first run with it live.

title: A Lean reply with no goals field is read as a closed proof
description:
lean-repl/apply-tactic computes closed? as (and (empty? errs) (empty? (:goals r))). send-command returns the REPL's JSON verbatim, so when a reply carries no goals key at all, (:goals r) is nil, (empty? nil) is true, and the proof is declared CLOSED. A missing field is read as an affirmative 'no goals remain'.

Three artifacts across two runs were confirmed this way, each on the single tactic , which adds a decidability instance and closes nothing:

  a#758  gen-24 B1 t9   lemma (B): a finite DAG admits a rank function
  a#759  gen-24 B2 t11  lemma (B) again, the supposedly independent second proof
  a#780  gen-25 B3 t29  TARGET 1: a directed cycle yields a balanced edge subset

a#758/a#759 were reported as 'proved twice, independently' and a#780 as closing the last gap in the correctness chain. All three are void. Both were seeded forward, so gen-25's pool carries them as inherited CONFIRMED results.

Note gen-24 B1.2.3 t48 used  as its first of 17 tactics and did NOT close, so the trigger is a property of the reply, not of the tactic.

Fix: a proof is closed only when the reply affirmatively reports an empty goals collection. An absent key means the harness cannot tell, which is not the same as done — the same rule the file already applies to warnings vs errors, where treating them alike 'is how sorry gets recorded as verified'.

run-command has the same shape at :ok (empty? errs) and should be checked.
close_reason: Fixed and field-validated: apply-tactic requires an affirmatively empty goal list. gen-27 hit the ambiguous reply 19 times, every one of which the old code would have recorded as a closed proof. The sibling defect in run-command is vf-k0v, now also fixed.

title: lean_search returns name-similarity noise as confident matches
description:
lean-search/search keeps any declaration sharing at least ONE token with the query — (when (pos? overlap) ...) — and render says 'No Mathlib declaration matched' only when the result set is completely empty. Against 215k declarations that essentially never happens, so every query returns a confident-looking list.

gen-25, first 29 turns: 14 lean_search, 12 fetch_artifact, 3 thesis, ZERO verification attempts across all three branches. Query 'finite directed graph cycle balanced indegree outdegree equal subset' returned Finite.subset and eventually_subset_of_finite — 2 of 8 terms. Query 'finite directed graph acyclic iff exists topological order rank function' returned order_lt_iff_exists and Function.Bijec...

The branch cannot tell noise from a hit, so it reasonably concludes the lemma exists and searches again with different words. progress-stalled fired 4 times and went unmet all 4. 28 of 29 turns are :neutral, so the loop costs nothing in either direction and the cull counter never moves.

Same class as the raw Lean errors: the harness returns something unhelpful with no signal that it is unhelpful. Add a relevance floor, and when nothing clears it say so — 'Mathlib may not have this, prove it directly' is far more useful than a list of near-misses. Keep the names visible but strip the false confidence, and tell the branch how many searches it has run without an attempt.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run. 40% relevance floor; below it the names still show with the overlap count and the advice to prove it directly.

title: same-claim refusal blocks review, which exists to re-examine proved ground
description:
already-proved (vf-cak) is consulted by claim-dedup, which review calls too. review operates on a claim the branch has ALREADY confirmed — its body reads (last (state/confirmed-artifacts branch)) — so a check that refuses claims already in the pool refuses review by construction, every time.

gen-23, first 197 turns: 8 same-claim refusals, 5 of them review. Each one cost a branch the independent cross-check of a result it had just verified.

Second hazard, not yet observed but live: consensus/engine-agreement counts DISTINCT engine kinds confirming a claim, on the stated grounds that independent empirical checks compose where opinions do not. Refusing verify_smt on a Lean-confirmed claim would suppress exactly that signal.

One rule covers both: refuse only when the attempted verification uses the SAME engine kind as the artifact that already carries the claim. review has no engine kind and is never refused; smt-on-lean is allowed and is evidence; smt-on-smt is the duplicate this was built to stop.

Also: the same-claim-refusal journal event omits :turn, so it cannot be joined to the turn it refused.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: refuse only a same-engine repeat. review has no engine kind and is never touched; smt-on-lean runs and counts as agreement. Confirmed live in gen-23 — 3 refusals after the deploy, all on verify_lean/verify_smt, none on review.

title: StringBuilder.append is quadratic in jolt, so JSON on long strings crawls
description:
MISDIAGNOSED WHEN FILED, corrected 2026-08-12. The original text blamed clojure.data.json and cited ~700 bytes/sec (2KB=2.9s, 8KB=10.6s, 32KB=44.7s). Those numbers do not reproduce and were measured over nREPL while gen-18 had a beam of 4 plus the Lean pool saturating the box; they are contention, not the parser.

Measured on an idle machine, data.json parses at 0.0003-0.0004 ms/char (~2.5 MB/s) when the payload is many short values, and stays flat. It degrades only as a SINGLE string value grows: 0.0025 ms/char at 2KB rising to 0.0068 at 64KB. That is superlinear in one value, not slow overall.

ROOT CAUSE, in jolt and not in veriframe: host/chez/java/host-static-classes.ss defined

  (cons "append" (lambda (self x . rest) (sb-set! self (string-append (sb-str self) (append-text x rest))) self))

Every append copied the whole accumulated buffer, so building an n-char string was O(n^2). StringWriter.write and PrintWriter's write-through to either had the same shape. data.json reads a quoted string one character at a time into a StringBuilder, which is why a long string value was the only shape that hurt.

Veriframe hits it in both directions. The largest real witness (88103 chars, a flat map whose countA value is one ~87KB SMT-LIB string) took 623ms to read and 672ms to write.

FIXED in jolt a1856fbe: appends cons onto a pending chunk list, joined only when something reads the buffer; length/isEmpty/count answer from a running total so they do not force the join. Verified by test/chez/string-builder-perf.ss (make sbperf), which asserts a scaling ratio rather than a wall-clock floor: 16.1x for 4x the appends before, 3.2x after. jolt unit clean, corpus 4323/4332 with 0 new divergence, cts 6078 pass matching baseline, printperf within guards.

Result for that witness: read 623ms -> 200ms, write 672ms -> 89ms. Per-char cost is now flat at ~0.0022 instead of climbing.

REMAINING: veriframe runs the Homebrew jolt binary (0.7.5), which has the old host files baked in, so it does not see the fix until jolt is rebuilt and installed.
acceptance_criteria: A 32KB document parses in single-digit milliseconds, and the hot paths use the fast parser.
close_reason: Root-caused to jolt's quadratic StringBuilder/StringWriter append and fixed there (jolt fix/stringbuilder-quadratic-append, c22ce774). Verified: sbperf 16.1x -> 3.2x scaling, jolt unit clean, corpus 4323/4332 with 0 new divergence, cts 6078 matching baseline, veriframe suite 240 tests/1171 assertions clean under the fixed binary. Run-detail endpoint 322.7s -> 3.2s. No veriframe code change was needed for either.

title: The coverage rung blocks on words when only numbers were ever the point
description:
Run 0d0c3560, wind-down: B4 and B4.3 have between them made eleven done attempts and cannot ship. After three rounds of widening the stopword list the refusals are down to one or two words each, and they are still refusals: 'formed', 'banked', 'tested', 'legitimately', 'listing', 'individual', 'concrete'. Each round surfaces new ordinary English. It does not converge, and it has cost this run something like forty turns.

The rung's own docstring says what it is for: 'Numbers matter most — an answer naming a size, a bound, or a witness has to have that number in the evidence.' The number check is exact, cheap, and has never produced a false positive. The word check is a lexical proxy for 'does the answer assert something unsupported', a question the audit already answers with semantics and in context, and which it answered PASS for every one of these attempts.

Fix: numbers block, words advise. Uncovered numbers refuse done exactly as now. Uncovered words are journalled and handed to the AUDIT prompt, where a model can weigh in context whether they assert anything the evidence does not support — which is the gate that should have been asking all along.

This is not defence-in-depth removed; it is a proxy retired in favour of the check it was standing in for.
acceptance_criteria: A number in no artifact still refuses done. An audited answer is never refused over an English word, and the words the lexical check would have flagged reach the audit and the journal.
close_reason: Closed

title: The coverage rung forbids the exact vocabulary the relevance rung demands
description:
B4 of run 0d0c3560 called done eight times between t31 and t50 and burned about twenty turns on it. Its audit PASSED at t49. Six of the eight refusals came from the uncovered-tokens rung, listing as unsupported assertions: stated, facts, computation, checked, against, found, together, asked, settled, establish, evidence, showed, search, finding, proving, supported, general, partial, whenever, conditional, branch, selection, cardinality.

Almost none of those is an assertion. They are the words a model uses to FRAME one, which is what the stopword list already exists to exempt, and the list was last extended for exactly this ('does', 'from', 'having', 'follow').

Three separate causes, all mine:

1. CONTRADICTION WITH THE NEW RELEVANCE RUNG. That rung tells a branch to state which questions it did not settle and what it established instead. An honest partial answer must NAME the thing it failed to establish, and that thing is by construction absent from the evidence, so the coverage rung refuses the answer for containing it. The two rungs cannot both be satisfied. Introduced this morning.

2. NO MORPHOLOGICAL TOLERANCE. Matching is str/includes? against the raw haystack, so 'residues' misses 'residue', 'enumeration' misses 'enumerating', and 'optimal-flow' misses 'optimal flow'. Same stemming hole found in state/claim-tokens earlier today.

3. MISSING FRAMING VOCABULARY in the stopword list.

Fix, keeping the gate's actual purpose intact — numbers stay matched exactly against artifacts only, because fabricated numbers are what this rung is for. Word tokens get morphological and hyphen tolerance, and may also be covered by the passing audit's own ESTABLISHED restatement.
acceptance_criteria: A branch whose audit has passed can ship an honestly-scoped partial answer without the coverage rung refusing it for words like 'settled' or 'establish', and a number appearing in no artifact is still refused.
close_reason: Closed

title: A rejected artifact never told the branch what was wrong
description:
encoding-faithful? returned a bare boolean and discarded the reviewer's reasoning. Every engine then showed the branch generic boilerplate ('Check every coefficient, bound and index set against the claim's wording'), and the failure log — which IS cross-branch — recorded 'z3 returned unsat (status unfaithful)'.

Observed live on the phase-unwrap run, twice over:
- The reviewer found a sign error in one divergence equation and named the fix exactly: change (+ (- k4) (- k7)) to (+ k4 (- k7)). The branch got the boilerplate and resubmitted the IDENTICAL artifact the next turn.
- A vacuous-unsat objection ('proves uniqueness, never asserts the candidate is feasible') was learned by B1.2 at turn 18 and repeated verbatim by B1.2.3 at turn 27, because the cross-branch failure log carried only the boilerplate.

So the judge was doing high-quality work — three distinct defect classes caught, often with an exact fix — and none of it reached anyone.

Fixed: encoding-faithful? returns {:ok? :reason}, where reason is the structural warnings or the judge's text. All five call sites (prolog, smt, template, lean, octave) quote it to the branch, and the smt failure reason carries it into the cross-branch log.
acceptance_criteria: A rejection shows the branch the actual objection, and the failure log carries it.
close_reason: Fixed and hot-reloaded into the live run over nREPL. Test: a-rejection-quotes-the-objection-to-the-branch-and-the-failure-log.

title: Prolog verify has no faithfulness check and records only the goal name
description:
gen-13 (6f6704f4) artifact 333, branch B3.3.3 turn 21, is CONFIRMED and FALSE. Claim: 'The q=105 layered condition ... has a satisfying assignment' for the 45 3,5,7-smooth moduli <= 2000. It would be a major result — it implies the mod-15 condition is satisfiable at N=2000, since a mod-15 class's relative density is the average of its seven mod-105 sub-classes.

The rule (added turn 20 as q105_n2000) posts its class constraints inside findall/3:

  findall(., (between(0,104,C), class_terms(...), scalar_product(Coefs,Bs,#>=,L)), _),
  labeling([ff],Flat).

findall/3 runs its goal in a separate context and undoes bindings AND constraint posts on completion, so every density constraint is discarded before labeling runs. What remains is 'Row ins 0..1, sum(Row,#=,1)' — pick one residue per modulus — which is trivially satisfiable. Hence 10 instant solutions with empty witnesses.

Demonstrated in swipl:
  X in 0..1, findall(_, (X #>= 5), _), label([X])   -> succeeds, X=0
  X in 0..1, X #>= 5, label([X])                    -> fails

Two harness defects:

1. The vf-slr faithfulness judge is wired only into verify_smt. verify (prolog), verify_lean, verify_octave and verify_template have no equivalent, and this is the identical failure mode the judge exists to catch.

2. The prolog artifact's code column records only the goal ('sat_105'), not the rule body that defines it. The definition lives in an earlier add_rule turn, so the artifact is not self-contained and cannot be audited from the artifacts table alone. Whatever check gets added must see the rule text, and crossover/seeding must carry it.

Impact: the false claim is confirmed in a live run and reachable by other branches through the shared artifact log, where it argues the mod-105 direction is a dead end. The truth is the opposite — mod-15 is verified unsat through N=1500 and mod-105 is finer still.
acceptance_criteria: An engine-confirmed prolog artifact carries the rules its goal depends on, and a would-be confirmation is checked against its claim the way verify_smt is.
close_reason: Fixed in 965b459: prolog artifacts carry the assert log with the goal, would-be confirmations go through the same faithfulness judge as verify_smt (with a note naming findall/3, forall/2 and \+ as contexts that undo constraint posts), and the ground-goal path no longer reaches :confirmed on the strength of merely succeeding. Tests cover all three. NOT YET DEPLOYED to the running server — needs a restart to take effect.

title: Branch that forks twice reissues a child id and kills the run
description:
spawn-children! named children (str parent-id "." (+ batch-index 2)), with no memory of an earlier fork. A branch that forks a second time reissues .2, the INSERT fails 'UNIQUE constraint failed: branches.run_id, branches.id', the exception escapes run-rounds and the run dies.

Killed both campaign runs:
- gen-11 (90336412): B1.2 spawned B1.2.2/B1.2.3 at turn 25; repopulate invited it at 02:33:48; it called branch_theses at 02:34:26; next round collided. Silent, because start-run! swallowed the throw — this is the crash vf-92l was filed for and could not identify.
- gen-12 (98d0423e): B2.2 spawned B2.2.2/B2.2.3 at turn 24, forked again at turn ~43, same collision. Diagnosed in minutes because the vf-92l fix journaled the message and type.

Not a corner case. Repopulation asks the strongest survivor to branch again, and the strongest survivor is the one that has already branched, so any run that loses width twice hits it.

Fixed in beam/child-ids: allocate from the ids already in the branches table, skipping taken suffixes and filling gaps. Reads the DB rather than branch state so a resumed run is also correct.
acceptance_criteria: A parent can fork twice; ids stay unique; tests cover the allocator and a live double fork.
close_reason: Fixed in eda36a4: beam/child-ids allocates from the branches table, skipping taken suffixes. Tests cover the allocator and a live double fork. This was also the unidentified gen-11 crash from vf-92l.

title: Beam crash leaves run marked 'running' forever; exception swallowed to stdout
description:
Run 90336412 (gen-11) stopped at 02:34:46 with status still 'running' and ended_at NULL.

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (an earlier version of this issue blamed a Chez GC handshake; that was wrong — it profiled an unrelated process, /tmp/prog.clj, a core.async test spinning at 100%. Verified since: jolt honours deref timeouts on both futures and promises).

What actually happened: beam/run! threw. Evidence:
- harness (jolt serve, pid 62370) is IDLE — 10:37 CPU over 3h, no outbound sockets, no engine subprocesses
- ZERO swipl processes, though every live branch holds a prolog session -> run!'s finally ran and disposed them
- neither finish-run! call site (beam.clj:521 completed, :538 failed) was reached, since status is still 'running'

The swallow is api/control.clj start-run!:

  (catch Throwable e
    (log/error "run failed:" (ex-message e))
    {:status :error :error (ex-message e)})

It logs to the process's stdout (a tty) and returns a value nobody reads — the future's value is never dereferenced. The run row is never updated, (swap! active dissoc run-id) is skipped so abort! still thinks it is live, and nothing is journaled. The only record of the actual exception is a line in the user's terminal scrollback.

So a crash is indistinguishable from a healthy long-running round: same status, same absence of events. That is the real defect — not the underlying throw, which is still unidentified.
acceptance_criteria: A non-yielding branch turn forfeits within the deadline and the beam continues.
close_reason: Fixed in e0d30c3: run-rounds journals run-error and marks the row failed before rethrowing; start-run! drops the dead handle; runs/stalled? plus last_progress_at exposed on the run endpoint. Verified against the dead gen-11 run, which now reports stalled=true instead of claiming to be running.

title: Judge confirms SMT claims whose encoding doesn't match the claim text
description:
Gen-11 shipped three confirmed artifacts (P500 a#308, P600 a#313, P1000 a#311) asserting 'no subcollection satisfies the mod-3 layered necessary condition'. All three encode the WRONG condition: a modulus m divisible by 3 lands entirely inside one class mod 3, so its relative density in that class is 3/m, but all three encodings give it L/m (same coefficient as a coprime modulus) against a threshold of L. That understates 3-divisible contributions 3x, making the system strictly harder to satisfy, so unsat proves something weaker than the claim.

Verified with Z3 on a regenerated pool (identical moduli/lcm to the artifacts): as-encoded is unsat for N=300,315,500,600,1000; corrected (3L/m) is unsat for 300,315 and SAT for 500,600,1000. So the claims are false, not merely unsupported.

B1.3 diagnosed this itself and honourably abandoned rather than ship. The gate did not.

Root cause: nothing checks that the submitted encoding faithfully represents the claim text. The judge reads claim + verdict; the linter checks syntax. A mis-scaled coefficient is invisible to both.
acceptance_criteria: An encoding-faithfulness check exists that would reject these three artifacts; the three gen-11 artifacts are marked refuted/retracted in the journal.
notes: Follow-up coverage issue is vf-djx (not vf-2ky as written in the close reason).
close_reason: Fixed across 965b459 and a701e51. Coverage: verify_smt and verify (prolog) now run deterministic structural checks BEFORE the LLM judge, and the judge after. Validated against the real artifacts — a#333, a#338, a#343 rejected; a#337, a#345 accepted; no false positives. Remaining gaps tracked in vf-2ky: verify_lean, verify_octave and verify_template are still judge-free, and refutations skip both layers.

title: A Lean REPL error message is discarded instead of shown to the branch
description:
apply-tactic treats a reply with no :goals key as unreadable and fails the tactic, which is correct — that reply shape used to be read as 'proof closed' and produced false confirmations (vf-4tw). But the reply is not unreadable. Its keys are [:message :ok]: the REPL is returning an error response and saying what went wrong, and the harness throws the text away.

gen-27 hit this 19 times. The branch sees 'The Lean REPL replied without a goal list, so the harness cannot tell whether the tactic closed the proof' and has no idea why. Same class as the raw Lean errors before the hints went in: the harness holds the diagnosis and does not pass it on.

My own message records the reply KEYS and not the message VALUE, which is the half that matters. Surface the message.

Worth noting the fix that produced this is validated by it: 19 replies that would previously have been recorded as closed proofs.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: when the REPL returns {:message ...} the message reaches the branch instead of a bare 'cannot tell'. Also confirms vf-4tw's value — 19 replies in gen-27 alone that the old code would have recorded as closed proofs.

title: Byte-identical proof code is re-verified because the judge compares prose
description:
already-proved asks a judge whether two CLAIMS state the same fact. The claim is prose, so two artifacts carrying the same theorem can be worded differently enough for a conscientious judge to call them distinct.

gen-27 a#809 and a#810: same branch B3.2, byte-identical code, both confirmed. The judge's reason: 'The first statement applies the decidable-equality hypothesis to both (1) and (2), while the second applies it only to (2); thus statement (1) differs in its hypotheses.' Careful reading of the prose, and wrong about the mathematics — the code is the same theorem.

That is the designed fail-closed bias (unsure means let it verify) producing a false negative, which costs a duplicate verification rather than a wrong credit, so the direction is right. But identical code needs no judgment: if a confirmed artifact from the SAME engine already carries this exact code, it is the same result whatever the claim says.

Check code identity before the judge. No model call, no ambiguity, and it cannot false-positive.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: an identical encoding from the same engine is settled before the judge is consulted. Whitespace-insensitive and nothing looser, so it cannot false-positive.

title: An artifact proved as an anonymous example cannot be cited by anything
description:
verify_lean accepts  and banks the result as a confirmed artifact. An example has no name, so no later proof can exact it, apply it, or reference it at all — the only way to use it is to prove it again.

That defeats the point of seeding. seed-from-run! carries code across generations precisely 'so a branch can re-confirm an inherited lemma in one cheap turn instead of reconstructing the encoding', and an anonymous declaration cannot be re-confirmed cheaply or built on.

25 confirmed Lean artifacts across the campaign are anonymous examples. gen-27 a#801 is one: a correct two-line proof of [a,c].Chain' r iff r a c, banked and unusable.

lint-lean lists example among the accepted declaration forms. Refuse it there — before Lean runs, same as the sorry check — with a message saying to name it. A theorem or lemma costs one word more and can be built on. There is no case in this harness where an anonymous example is the right choice for verify_lean, since verify_lean always banks what it proves.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run: the lint refuses an anonymous example when no named declaration sits alongside, naming theorem/lemma as the fix. Caught before Lean runs, same as the sorry check.

title: lean_search weights a match on iff the same as a match on transgen
description:
Scoring counts matched tokens equally, so a query's rare and discriminating words carry no more weight than Mathlib's name-particles. In the 215,781-declaration index: iff appears in 17,610 names (8.16%), mem in 8,441, exists in 3,960 — against transgen in 30 (0.01%) and acyclic in 10. A match on iff is roughly 600x less informative than a match on transgen and scores the same.

gen-27, first 58 turns: 36 lean_search calls, 37 distinct queries, so branches are exploring rather than looping. But 'Relation.TransGen iff exists list Chain' returned mem_closure_iff_exists_list — sharing iff, exists, list for 50% overlap, clearing the 40% relevance floor added in vf-f5c while missing every word that mattered.

Raising the floor is the wrong fix; it would suppress genuine short matches. Weight each matched token by inverse document frequency computed from the index itself, and make the relevance floor a fraction of the query's total IDF mass rather than of its token count. Self-maintaining, no hand-curated stoplist.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run. Matches weighted by IDF computed from the index in one memoised pass; the relevance floor is now a share of the query's IDF mass. Verified on the gen-27 query that prompted it — correctly reported as no good match — while a genuine query still returns its matches.

title: Campaign: run gen-27 onward until Q-1 is settled, at least 5 more generations
description:
Standing directive from 2026-08-15: when a generation finishes without cracking Q-1, formulate and launch the next one. At least five more runs beyond gen-26 unless a full solution lands sooner.

Per generation:
1. Read the final answer and verify it independently — read proof BODIES, not confirmed labels. gen-24 and gen-25 both had artifacts marked confirmed whose entire proof was the tactic  (vf-4tw).
2. Quarantine any claim later found void so it does not seed forward.
3. Update docs/phase-unwrapping-3.md with what moved.
4. Formulate the next run from what is actually open, naming inherited artifacts by content so nothing is re-proved.
5. Fix harness problems seen along the way and deploy over nREPL; never restart a server with a run in flight.

Current position after gen-26 (in flight): the correctness chain needs TARGET 1 only — a support that is not acyclic contains a nonempty balanced edge subset. TARGET 2 (a finite DAG admits a rank function) was genuinely proved in gen-26, a#788, verified by hand. Beyond that: the arc-subdivision reduction theorem is unproved, and the arbitrary-instance case needs a log-S-bounded convex min-cost flow subroutine or a hardness result.

A full solution means: a polynomial-time algorithm for ARBITRARY instances with a verified chain, or a hardness proof. An instance-class-only result is a partial answer and the campaign continues.
notes:
DRIFT PATTERN, three generations running: a branch hits the hard target, backs off, and spends its remaining turns re-confirming already-settled results, then ships a partial built from those. gen-24 and gen-26 used small-instance SMT probes; gen-27 B3.2 used cross-engine re-verification of inherited bounds (a#811, a#812) after failing step 3 at t131, and ran an audit at t135 to test shipping.

The harness permits it by design — the same-engine dedup rule allows cross-engine confirmation because consensus/engine-agreement counts distinct engines as real evidence, which is right when a result is doubted. None of these were doubted.

gen-28's formulation now says re-verifying inherited work is not progress, and asks a branch that is beaten by TARGET 1 to say which step beat it instead.

title: Argument-shape faults are charged to the counter that decides whether a branch lives
description:
fail always returns :category :failure, and every argument-validation complaint goes through it. A branch that mis-serialized its arguments has produced no claim and tested no line of inquiry, but the harness records it as a failed verification and it counts toward the cull.

Measured across gen-22/23/24: 213 failure-category turns, of which ~21 are pure argument-shape complaints (10%). 16 are branch_theses emitting the byte-identical ' must be a non-empty array of {goal, subClaims, technique} objects.' gen-24 culled 5 of 8 branches, several 'after 3 consecutive failures'.

This is the vf-jki pattern in a fifth place: fences, expectedVerdict, proof_start, engine outages, and now argument shape. The precedents are already in the file — unavailable is :neutral because 'a branch cannot answer for an outage and must not spend cull budget on one', and a malformed fence is :mechanics because 'the branch produced no claim, so there is nothing here to hold against its line of inquiry'.

Argument shape is the same: :mechanics, so the count still bounds a branch looping on malformed calls but does not read as evidence against its mathematics.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed mid-run. Argument-shape faults are :mechanics; the count still bounds a branch looping on bad calls but no longer reads as a failed line of inquiry. Also covers vague-claim, which is refused before any engine runs.

title: safe-state is missing from the settle case, so it can never be met
description:
arbiter/settle dispatches on gate in a case whose fallthrough is false. Every gate is listed except :safe-state, so its prediction — 'the branch retracts, changes technique, or ships what it has' — is never evaluated as true, expires, and is recorded :unmet.

Across gen-22/23/24 it is 0 met / 2 unmet. That reads as a gate the model ignores, when in fact the harness never checked. Same shape as the failures charged to the cull counter in vf-jki: a tally that blames the branch for something the harness did not measure.

Observable proxies for its prediction already exist as tool calls: retract_rule (retracts), thesis (changes technique), done/give_up (ships what it has), review.

Fix the case, and make it impossible for a gate to be silently unsettleable — a gate whose name is absent from the dispatch should fail loudly in tests rather than settle unmet forever.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed. safe-state settles on retract_rule/thesis/done/give_up/review; a coverage test now walks the gate table so a gate without a settle rule fails in tests.

title: Lean rejections hand back raw engine output with no guidance
description:
verify_lean's rejection message is the raw Lean error plus one generic sentence ('That is a problem with the proof, not evidence about the claim'). The model gets no reading of what the error class means, and the same classes recur across generations.

34 Lean engine failures across gen-22/23/24:
  8  linarith/omega failed
  7  syntax / unexpected token
  7  unsolved goals
  4  failed to synthesize instance
  3  rewrite pattern not found
  2  unknown identifier/constant
  2  no goals to be solved

Every one of the 8 linarith/omega failures is a goal that MULTIPLIES unknowns — 8*E^3*V^2 < E*S*(2*E*(...)), 125*E^5*V^4 < (2*(E*S)+1)*(...) — against tactics that are linear-only by construction. The run is deriving polynomial work bounds from E <= 2V and S <= 2V, which needs products of hypotheses: nlinarith, or explicit mul_le_mul chains.

Most syntax failures are 'unexpected token in; expected ,' — Mathlib 4 writes the binder as (sum) x IN-SYMBOL s and deprecated the 'in' spelling that dominates training data.

Instance failures are equally diagnosable: GetElem on a function means f[i] was written where f i was meant; Fintype X has Lean's own deriving hint; DecidablePred wants Classical or a DecidableRel binder.

Add a hint keyed on the error class, appended to the rejection. Name the fault and the tactic that addresses it; do not do the mathematics — same discipline as  and .
close_reason: Nine error-class hints shipped and deployed into gen-24, ranked by turns lost across gen-22/23/24. Unmatched errors deliberately get no hint.

title: Assemble the arc-subdivision reduction theorem
description:
Every runtime bound in gen-23 and gen-24 is stated as conditional on the reduction of each separable convex prefix subproblem to a unit-capacity min-cost flow on the subdivided network. The ingredients are proved — nondecreasing marginal costs (a#828), the telescoping identity (a#830), separable discrete convexity (a#821) — but the reduction theorem itself is not.

Until it is assembled, every polynomial work bound in the campaign rests on an unverified hypothesis.

title: Document the phase-unwrapping instance-class result once lemma (A) lands
description:
Once (A) — directed cycle in the sign-oriented support yields a nonzero sign-aligned circulation — is engine-verified, the correctness half of Q-1 closes end to end: no directed cycle, rank function (a#758/a#759), |k_e| <= S (a#745), box faithfulness, and the greedy prefix selector returning exactly the three-stage flow including the lexicographic tie-break over the exponential stage-2 face.

Combined with gen-23's S <= 2V for grid dual graphs, that is a polynomial-time algorithm for the instance class that actually ships in InSAR and MRI field mapping. Write it up: the chain, which artifact carries each link, and the independent checks (3,215-instance selector agreement and box tightness; E<=2V, |b_v|<=2, and both runtime bounds re-derived by hand).

Be explicit that this is the instance-class result, NOT Q-1 as posed. See the sibling issues for the general case.

title: Two branches proving the same lemma in different words both pay for it
description:
claims/normalize and consensus/normalize-claim are both spelling-level: lowercase and strip punctuation. A lemma restated with renamed variables is a different key, so the registry never sees it.

Measured on gen-22's 29 confirmed artifacts, 4-gram Jaccard:
- a#689 / a#693, Jaccard 1.00 — caught by the exact key (vf-3k4 wires the tool that missed it)
- a#687 / a#689, Jaccard 0.28 — the SAME coefficient-feasibility lemma with B renamed to D = E*R, and both on branch B3. One branch proved it twice.
- a#712 / a#717, Jaccard 0.19 — a#717's claim text literally reads "(re-verified on this branch)". The model knew and did it anyway, so surfacing the neighbour is not enough on its own.

Lexical matching found 1 of at least 3. No threshold fixes this: the pairs differ in wording precisely where they agree in content.

Design constraint that shapes the fix: a false 'same claim' would credit a branch with a verdict it never earned, which is worse than the duplicate work. So the judge must NOT auto-credit. Prefilter with FTS over the confirmed pool (which covers seeded artifacts too, unlike the in-memory registry), ask the judge once whether any candidate is the same statement, and on a match REFUSE the verification with the neighbour's exact claim text and id attached — the branch is the only party that knows what it meant, and fetch_artifact already exists for it to pull the statement.

Refusal must be :mechanics, not :failure. The branch's line of inquiry is sound; it aimed at something already done. Charging it to the cull counter is the vf-jki mistake again.
close_reason: Judge-gated same-claim check shipped; scoping bug found and fixed in vf-met. Field-proven in gen-23: 8 refusals, 15 comparisons, reasoning on hypotheses and conclusions rather than wording.

title: The claim registry is wired to 2 of 6 verdict paths, so it never fires
description:
claims/try-claim! implements the UCLA claim protocol correctly: one branch holds a claim while it verifies, every other branch is served the verdict instead of paying for it again. Only verify_template and review consult it, and only those two ever populate it.

gen-22, 97 slow verifications: verification-dedup-hit fired 0 times. verify_template was never called; review was called 16 times and no two branches reviewed the same claim string. Meanwhile proof_start ran 34 times, verify_lean 23, audit 12, verify_smt 6, verify_octave 6 — none of them visible to the registry in either direction.

Measured on the 68 slow verifications carrying a claim: exactly one byte-identical cross-branch repeat, B3:t11 and B2.2:t17, both verify_smt, both ran z3 on the same claim. That is precisely the case the registry exists for, on a tool that does not ask it.

Cross-generation is separately fine: 0 of the 68 re-proved any of the 14 seeded claims at 4-gram Jaccard >= 0.6, so the ledger and shared-artifact blocks are carrying that load.

Wire verify_smt, verify_lean and verify_octave in. Only a verdict ABOUT THE CLAIM may settle it — a rejected proof, a sorry, or an unfaithful encoding says nothing about whether the claim is true (verify_lean's own comment makes this argument for the artifact table) and must release, or one branch's bad encoding locks a true claim out for the rest of the run.
notes: Close reason above was pasted from vf-mxm and is wrong. Correct status: fixed and deployed, tests green, but NOT field-proven — no branch attempted a slow verification between the deploy and the end of gen-22, so verification-dedup-hit never fired. First real evidence will come from gen-23.
close_reason: Fixed, deployed and confirmed live: 3 no-calls since deploy, all 3 recovered on the next turn opening inside the fence. Baseline was 41% of no-calls followed by another no-call.

title: A turn that emits no tool call should be prefilled into the fence on the next turn
description:
gen-22 B1 spent 24 of its 44 turns on __no_call__ / __parse_error__ — more than half the branch's budget produced nothing. Across the whole run 59 of 286 turns (20.6%) were mechanics, plus 50 turn-retries for 'truncated before any tool call', each a full duplicate model call.

The current corrective is a prose message ('[harness] No tool-call block in your response'). It demonstrably does not work: B1 received it 24 times. One turn produced 109,360 characters at the 32,768-token cap and still emitted no fence.

The mechanism to fix this already exists. arbiter/prefill-for ends a request mid-fence so the model cannot answer in prose, and it is plumbed through call-model, fence/parse-tool-call and fence/reattach. It is only ever set from a gate decision, so it never reaches the branch that most needs it.

Set the bare fence prefill on the no-call path. Bare, not tool-named: which tool to call is the branch's decision, not the harness's.
close_reason: Fixed, deployed and confirmed live: 3 no-calls since deploy, all 3 recovered on the next turn opening inside the fence. Baseline was 41% of no-calls followed by another no-call.

title: Give each branch a knowledge ledger: what is settled, what is ruled out, details on request
description:
A branch currently learns what the run knows by reading its own narrative and a 5-entry FTS-ranked sample of siblings' confirmed claims. That is a transcript, not a state. What a branch needs in order to choose its next move is the opposite shape: a short standing list of what is established and what is closed, with the details fetchable rather than inlined.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENTS SAY THIS SHOULD AND SHOULD NOT BE.

Not a context-size fix. No branch in 112 measured has exceeded ~53k effective tokens; the worst is 86 turns at 52,778, and 96.5% of stored assistant_text is reasoning already stripped before resend. Pruning the transcript would be solving a problem the harness does not have, and would cost resume fidelity and the branch's working memory.

It is a signal-to-noise and duplicate-work fix. gen-20 had three branches prove the same scalarization lemma while each was served the others' claims five times (vf-8wp). And the ledger is cheap: gen-20's entire confirmed knowledge is 1,495 chars of claims — under 400 tokens — against B3's ~50k-char transcript. Even gen-17's 97 confirmed artifacts would be roughly 13KB, ~3k tokens, and COMPLETE rather than a top-5 sample.

SHAPE.

  ## Established (engine-verified)
  - [a#12 lean/slow] scalarization yields the lex minimum under H > K*Qmax + Lrange
  - [a#17 smt/fast]  the dipole square's stage-2 set is exactly {(0,0,1,1),(1,1,0,0)}
  ## Ruled out
  - [a#09 smt/fast]  zero TOTAL SIGNED weight does NOT imply optimality-preserving
  ## Open
  - ...

Regenerated every turn from the artifacts table, which already stores all of it — no new storage, and it cannot drift from the record. Ids are the links: a branch that wants the encoding asks for it, so the code costs a turn only when it is wanted rather than riding in every block.

Depends on refutations being shareable at all (vf-*), which is the missing half.
design:
Complete rather than FTS-sampled, for statuses whose population is small — confirmed and refuted are tens of entries, not thousands, and a sample defeats the purpose: the whole value is that a branch can trust the absence of a line. Keep the existing FTS-ranked block for CODE (vf-8wp) where relevance ranking is right because the payload is large.

The ledger is a view, not a second source of truth. Everything in it is derived per turn from artifacts rows; nothing is written to maintain it.

Include the branch's OWN artifacts, unlike the shared block which excludes them. Re-reading one's own established facts as a list is exactly the point — the alternative is scanning an 80-turn narrative for them.

Needs a fetch-by-id tool so the ids are actionable rather than decorative.
acceptance_criteria: A branch's context carries a complete, current list of what the run has established and ruled out, in under ~3k tokens, with ids that can be expanded on request.

title: Refutations are never shared: 127 disproven claims, none visible to any branch
description:
loop/shareable? admits an artifact into the shared pool only when (= :confirmed (:claim-status artifact)). Across the project's history the artifacts table holds:

  confirmed    398        <- shared
  refuted      127        <- NEVER shared
  unfaithful   110        <- correctly withheld, the encoding did not establish the claim
  existential   19        <- never shared
  empirical     16        <- never shared
  ambiguous      9        <- never shared

So a branch is told what siblings have PROVEN and never what they have DISPROVEN. Nothing stops it spending turns on a line another branch already closed, and nothing in its context would reveal that it had.

A refutation is arguably worth more per token than a confirmation for deciding what to try next: a confirmation adds one fact, a refutation prunes a whole direction. gen-17 refuted the natural strengthening of the zero-weight-cycle condition and gen-18 refuted the literal residual-network criterion — both are exactly the kind of thing a sibling would otherwise re-attempt.

MEASURED CONTEXT (why this is the fix rather than context pruning): across 112 branches in the project's history no branch has ever exceeded ~53k tokens of effective context, and the worst case is 86 turns at 52,778. 96.5% of stored assistant_text is reasoning that message/strip-think-blocks already drops before resend. So context exhaustion is not the problem and pruning the transcript is premature; the problem is that the knowledge which IS carried is half-missing and buried in narrative.
design:
Extend shareable? beyond :confirmed, but not to everything. :refuted belongs in — it is engine-established and it prunes. :unfaithful must stay out, since the encoding did not establish the claim and sharing it would spread a claim nothing verified. :empirical and :existential are judgement calls worth deciding explicitly rather than by omission.

The render must keep the verdict attached and unmissable — a refuted claim rendered like a confirmed one is worse than not sharing it. Suggest separate sections rather than a status tag on a line, so a skimming model cannot merge them.
acceptance_criteria: A branch can see what siblings have ruled out, with the verdict impossible to confuse for a confirmation.
close_reason:
Built as one mechanism instead of three. journal/ledger reads the artifacts table — which already has claim_status where shared_artifacts does not — so refutations become visible with no migration and no second sharing path; that is vf-0tk solved via the ledger rather than by widening shareable?, which I had filed. Complete rather than FTS-sampled, since the value is that a branch can trust the absence of a line. Two sections so a refutation cannot read as a confirmation. fetch_artifact makes the ids actionable, :neutral so a lookup cannot clear a failure count, run-scoped, and works on refuted artifacts where the encoding is what shows why the line is closed.

THE PART THAT NEARLY WENT WRONG: the block is appended every turn, so a naive wiring accumulates one copy per turn — gen-17's ledger over an 80-turn branch would have been 854,800 chars / 211k tokens, four times the largest context ever recorded. message/strip-stale-ledgers drops all but the newest on the way to the wire, following the strip-think-blocks precedent; the branch keeps every copy so the journal and resume stay faithful. 80 turns now costs 10,642 chars instead of 854,800. Claims capped at 180 chars with the full statement one fetch away: gen-18's ledger 6,795 -> 3,805 tokens, gen-20's 428.

264 tests, 1324 assertions, 0 failures.

title: A branch repeats an identical failed call and gets the identical message back
description:
55% of gen-20's failures are the same four mistakes made over and over. Of 53 recorded failures:

  11  proof_start  'The theorem statement did not elaborate: unexpected token ...'
   9  __no_call__  'No ```tool-call block in your response.'   (pre-vf-jki, now :mechanics)
   5  proof_start  'Missing required argument(s): claim, theorem.'
   4  proof_step   'No proof is open. Call proof_start first.'

B1 — the branch that had independently rediscovered the greedy lex characterisation, this run's best idea — was culled on exactly this. Its last twelve turns are proof_start failing five times, three of them with the byte-identical missing-argument error, interleaved with proof_step failing because no proof was open. It called proof_step, was told to call proof_start, called proof_start wrong, was told, and went round again. Thirteen real failures against one success, and the harness said the same sentence each time.

The cull was CORRECT — these were genuine failures, not the mechanics miscount of vf-jki, which is working. The problem is upstream: nothing notices that a branch is repeating itself, so the harness's response to the fifth identical mistake is identical to its response to the first.

tools.clj:89 builds the missing-argument error as a bare list of names — 'Missing required argument(s): claim, theorem.' — with no indication of the shape expected. A model that did not understand the call the first time learns nothing new the second.

This reframes vf-ap8, which proposed repetition detection over the model's PROSE. The measured repetition is in tool calls and harness errors, which are structured, already journalled, and far cheaper to compare than free text.
design:
Two cheap moves, both narrower than a general loop detector:

1. Escalate on repeat. When the same branch produces the same tool plus the same error class N times, change the message: include the tool's argument schema and a correct example call rather than restating the complaint. The harness knows the schema; it just does not show it. This is a strictly better use of the turn the branch is going to spend anyway.

2. Enrich the argument error at source. tools.clj:89 already knows which names are absent; naming their types and showing a minimal valid call costs nothing and addresses the single most repeated failure directly.

Deliberately NOT a general text-similarity detector: tool name plus error message is an exact comparison over data already in the turns table, so this needs no threshold tuning and cannot fire on an honest retry that changed something.
acceptance_criteria: A branch that makes the same failing call twice gets a materially different, more specific message the second time, and the repeat-failure share of a run drops from the 55% measured here.
close_reason: Two fixes, both TDD. (1) missing-argument errors now show the call they wanted — 'A call to `proof_start` looks like: {"name": "proof_start", "args": {"claim": "<claim>", "theorem": "<theorem>"}}' — built from the tool name and required keys the function is already handed, so no schema registry. (2) state/repeating-failure? compares the last two turns on exact (tool, error) and the loop appends an escalation telling the branch to change the call or the technique. Exact comparison, no threshold, cannot fire on a retry that changed anything or on a branch that succeeded in between. Resume does not replay the per-turn :error — noted in resume.clj's fidelity contract, because the turns table holds the ESCALATED text which would not compare equal and would break the detection it was meant to restore. 254 tests, 1267 assertions, 0 failures.

title: Make fence parsing accept a response whose opening fence was prefilled
description:
Second half of vf-tso, and the part most likely to break silently.

fence/parse-tool-call matches on fence-re, #"(?s)```tool-call\s*\r?\n(.*?)```" — it requires the opening ```tool-call marker. When the opener is sent as an assistant prefill the model does not repeat it, so the response body starts mid-fence and every prefilled turn would parse as a no-call. That would turn a fix for __no_call__ into a generator of them.

The parse path needs the sent prefix reattached before matching, which means the prefix has to travel with the response rather than being inferred.
design: TDD. Tests first, and they are the specification: a response that omits the opener parses correctly when the prefix is known; a response that DOES repeat the opener (models vary) must not produce a doubled fence; a response with no prefill still parses exactly as today. The multi-fence and repair paths must behave identically either way, since both feed mechanics counters that gate nothing but tune repair budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Prefilled and non-prefilled responses both parse, with no change to mechanics signals for the non-prefilled case.
close_reason: Implemented and tested. Adapter protocol gained prefill-support?; the OpenAI-family adapter appends the prefix as a trailing assistant message flagged :prefix true, and only for DeepSeek — plain OpenAI, local and Ollama declare false and produce byte-identical bodies to today. client/chat now names :prefill in its opts, which it did not, so without that the whole path would have been dead code; there is a test pinning it. fence/parse-tool-call takes an opts map and reattaches the prefix before matching, skipping reattachment when the model repeated the opener itself. Non-prefilled parsing is unchanged, asserted by equality against the no-opts arity. 252 tests, 1255 assertions, 0 failures.

title: Add prefill support to the Adapter protocol and the OpenAI adapter
description:
First half of vf-tso. Give the adapter layer the ability to send an assistant prefix, without changing behaviour for any provider that does not support one.

Add a capability predicate to the Adapter protocol (default false) and honour a :prefill option in chat-body by appending {:role "assistant" :content <prefix>} as the final message. llm/client.clj's chat currently threads :max-tokens, :temperature and :max-retries through its opts map; :prefill goes the same way. Providers that do not advertise support ignore it entirely and take today's path.

Kept deliberately separate from the parse-side change (vf-*) because they fail differently: this one fails as a rejected request, that one as a parse error on every prefilled turn.
design: TDD. Tests first: an adapter advertising no support produces a body byte-identical to today's; an adapter advertising support appends exactly one trailing assistant message; the option is absent from the body when the caller does not pass it.
acceptance_criteria: chat-body emits the prefix only for adapters that advertise support, and existing provider tests are unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented and tested. Adapter protocol gained prefill-support?; the OpenAI-family adapter appends the prefix as a trailing assistant message flagged :prefix true, and only for DeepSeek — plain OpenAI, local and Ollama declare false and produce byte-identical bodies to today. client/chat now names :prefill in its opts, which it did not, so without that the whole path would have been dead code; there is a test pinning it. fence/parse-tool-call takes an opts map and reattaches the prefix before matching, skipping reattachment when the model repeated the opener itself. Non-prefilled parsing is unchanged, asserted by equality against the no-opts arity. 252 tests, 1255 assertions, 0 failures.

title: Force the tool-call fence with an assistant prefill instead of asking for it
description:
__no_call__ — a turn where the model emits no ```tool-call fence at all — is veriframe's dominant mechanical failure. gen-20 produced 7 of them in its first 26 turns, and they contributed to culling 2 of 5 branches before the beam had done any work (vf-jki). The harness currently handles this after the fact: it reports the problem back, counts it, and eventually bounds the branch. Nothing stops it happening.

There is a cheap lever the harness does not pull. Because tool calls are a fenced JSON block in free text rather than provider-native calls (see the llm.fence ns docstring for why), the model can always answer in prose instead. Appending an assistant message containing the opening fence — {:role "assistant" :content "```tool-call\n"} — forces continuation inside the fence and removes prose as an option. DeepSeek supports prefix completion; support varies across OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so it has to be an adapter capability with a fallback to today's behaviour.

The second reason to want this is vf-9sa. Gate predictions in gen-19 settled 4 met to 22 unmet, and the pattern there is that gates which WITHHOLD something change behaviour while gates which SUGGEST something do not — the audit gate's 14 refusals redirected work, milestone went 0-for-4 and tier-escalation 0-for-4. A prefill is a withholding mechanism. It is the missing lever that would let a nudge gate actually bind.

The targeted form is better than a blanket one: when a gate fires carrying a prediction, prefill the fence AND the predicted tool name — ```tool-call\n{\"name\": \"review\" — converting a suggestion into a constraint without touching gate budgets or priorities.
design:
Adapter capability, never a global. Add a prefill-support predicate to the Adapter protocol defaulting to false; chat-body appends the assistant message only when the caller passes :prefill and the adapter advertises support. Every other provider stays on the current path.

The parse path needs care: with a prefill the response will not repeat the opening fence, and fence/parse-tool-call matches on the ```tool-call opener, so the prefix has to be reattached before matching or every prefilled turn reads as a parse error. That is the failure mode to write a test for first.

Prefill must not mask a real problem. A model that cannot produce a well-formed call inside a forced fence is still failing, and the mechanics counters (vf-jki) must keep seeing it.
acceptance_criteria: A gate firing with a predicted tool can force that tool's fence on the next turn; __no_call__ rate drops measurably; providers without prefix support are unaffected.
close_reason: Duplicate of vf-mxm, fixed and field-proven: consecutive no-calls fell from 41% to 22%.

title: A malformed tool-call fence counts as a verification failure and culls the branch
description:
gen-20 B2 was culled at turn 6 having called thesis and lean_search and nothing else. Its other four turns produced no ```tool-call block at all. Each was recorded category='failure' (loop.clj:247) and fed to state/record-outcome, the same counter the cull gate reads — so three consecutive malformed fences killed a fifth of the beam before the branch ever made a substantive claim.

The reason it died with: 'culled after 3 consecutive failures; the critic scored the line a dead end'. The critic had no line to score.

loop.clj already draws exactly this distinction one branch up, for a provider error: 'A provider failure is not the branch's fault and must not count against it as a verification failure.' A fence the model malformed is the same kind of fault, and the branch already tracks mechanics separately (state.clj:51, explicitly 'Never verification or progress signals').

PRECEDENT: state.clj's record-outcome docstring records the same incident class from gen-18 — B1 made three malformed tool calls, recovered, ran three clean Octave sessions, and was culled on a counter last incremented three turns earlier. The fix then was to let neutral turns decay the counter. That was a partial fix; B2 shows it was not enough, because B2 never got far enough to earn a decay.
design:
Separated the counter rather than softening it. Softening alone would be a different bug: the mechanics map feeds only the capability tier and gates nothing, and turns-since-progress feeds only progress-stalled — a nudge gate gen-19 settled 0-for-2 (vf-9sa) — so with neither counter moving, a branch emitting nothing but garbage would hold a beam slot to the turn budget.

- New :mechanics category. record-outcome increments :consecutive-mechanics-failures and leaves :consecutive-failures alone; any well-formed call clears the mechanics tally, since the branch has shown it can work the protocol whatever the call then did.
- cull-or-keep gains its own arm at 2x cull-threshold with an honest reason naming the fence, not the critic.
- journal records category 'mechanics' so the record can tell a branch that was wrong from one that could not format a fence. Column is unconstrained TEXT; GUI renders the string through (or category "?") with no dispatch to break.
- All accessors nil-safe ((fnil inc 0) / (or ... 0)) so branches already in flight survive the hot reload.
acceptance_criteria: B2's exact turn sequence does not cull; a branch emitting only malformed fences is still bounded; the cull reason names the real cause.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed over nREPL into the running gen-20 without interrupting it. 248 tests, 1215 assertions, 0 failures. Verified live: record-outcome on B2's exact sequence gives consecutive-failures 0, mechanics 3 (under the 6 threshold), and is nil-safe for the four branches already in flight. B2 itself stays culled — a culled branch cannot be reopened and the beam no longer holds it — so gen-20 runs at 4 branches instead of 5.

title: The GUI reported a failed start for a run that was starting fine
description:
Clicking start run in the UI showed an error while the same request succeeded over curl.

CAUSE. gui.api set :socket-timeout 10000 for every call. POST /v1/runs does not answer when the run row is written: api.control/start-run! blocks on (deref promised 30000), and beam/run! only calls on-start after opening every branch —

  run-id (runs/start-run! conn {...})        ; row committed, started_at set
  _ (when seed-run (artifacts/seed-from-run! ...))
  initial (mapv #(open-branch! ctx ...) (range width))
  (when on-start (on-start run-id))          ; response released here

so the server is allowed 30s and the client gave up at 10. Measured: 47ms on an idle machine, 21095ms moments later with the system busy. curl has no such limit, which is why the endpoint 'worked'.

Worse than a spurious error: the row is already committed and the beam keeps going, so the user was told the run failed AND left with a live run consuming provider spend. Reproduced exactly — GUI client returned 'Read timed out' while run 60381dbb was created and ran on.

FIXED. gui.api/start-timeout-ms is 40000, deliberately above the server's own 30s budget, and POST takes a per-call override (branch-detail already did this with 45s). Covered by gui_api_test — the assertion is that start-run!'s socket timeout exceeds 30000, so it cannot silently drift back under the server's window. Verified end to end against a live server: a start that took 21095ms now succeeds.

FOLLOW-UP worth considering separately: on-start fires after the whole beam is open, which is what makes this endpoint slow and variable. api.control/start-run! documents itself as returning 'immediately'. Moving on-start to just after the row insert would make it actually immediate, at the cost of handing out an id for a run whose branches do not exist yet.
close_reason: Fixed and verified end to end: start-timeout-ms 40000 outlasts the server's 30s window, gui_api_test asserts it stays above 30000, and a 21095ms start now succeeds where it previously returned 'Read timed out'.

title: veriframe runs the Homebrew jolt, which predates the StringBuilder fix
description:
The quadratic-append fix (vf-gff) lives in jolt's host/chez/java sources, which the standalone binary bakes in at build time. `which jolt` resolves to /opt/homebrew/bin/jolt -> ../Cellar/jolt/0.7.5/bin/jolt, so every normal veriframe invocation — jolt serve, jolt -M:test, jolt -M:gui — still runs the old quadratic code.

Measured under each, same DB, same 1154801-byte run-detail response: 322.7s on the Homebrew binary against 3.2s on the freshly built one.

Until jolt is rebuilt and installed, none of the win reaches a real run. Deciding HOW is an environment call, not something to do silently: 'make install' writes to $PREFIX/bin (~/.local/bin by default) which would shadow or diverge from the Homebrew-managed copy, and bumping the Homebrew formula is a separate release step. A build exists at ~/src/jolt-lang/jolt/target/release/jolt and can be used directly in the meantime.
acceptance_criteria: A jolt carrying c22ce774 is what `jolt` resolves to, and the run-detail endpoint measures in seconds rather than minutes through the HTTP server.
close_reason: jolt 0.7.6 is installed (Cellar/jolt/0.7.6, symlinked at /opt/homebrew/bin/jolt) and carries a1856fbe — the StringBuilder fix rode into main on PR #593. Verified against the installed binary: run-detail 322740ms -> 3344ms in-process and 3.33s through HTTP, 88KB witness read 352ms / write 255ms, veriframe suite 240 tests / 1171 assertions clean.

title: The run-detail endpoint was slow serializing its response, not parsing it
description:
The run-detail endpoint was slow, but NOT for the reason first filed. The original text blamed get-run parsing witnesses only to re-encode them and attributed 53s of a 64s endpoint to that round trip. Measured component by component against a live server on an idle box (2026-08-12), every data-gathering step is fast:

  get-run row      1 ms
  last-progress    2 ms
  stalled?         6 ms
  branches (15)   10 ms
  run-metrics    300 ms
  artifacts (122) 58 ms
  gate-tally       1 ms
  interventions    1 ms

That is ~380ms total. The cost is entirely in serializing the response: json/write-str over the assembled 1.15MB body. So the parse-then-re-encode framing was wrong; the write direction was the problem, and both were the same underlying defect — jolt's quadratic StringBuilder/StringWriter append (vf-gff).

This is why vf-8g2 was made to depend on vf-gff rather than fixed on its own: changing the response shape would have been a GUI-visible contract change that the root-cause fix made unnecessary.

AFTER vf-gff (jolt a1856fbe), same run, same machine, in-process:
  build-body  193 ms
  write-str  3052 ms
  total      3245 ms   (1154801 bytes)

against >300s before (curl timed out at 300s). No veriframe change was needed.

Residual, not yet chased: 1.15MB in 3.05s is ~380 KB/s, while the single 88KB witness now writes at ~1 MB/s. Nested structure costs more per node than one long string, so this may be ordinary per-node overhead rather than anything left over — but it has not been measured, and the endpoint is no longer pathological either way.
acceptance_criteria: /v1/runs/<id> returns in under a second on a run with 120+ artifacts, with the response shape either preserved or the GUI updated in the same change.
notes:
Exact A/B, same DB, same 1154801-byte response, in-process (no HTTP):

  old jolt    build-body 205 ms   write-str 322535 ms   total 322740 ms
  fixed jolt  build-body 193 ms   write-str   3052 ms   total   3245 ms

write-str 322.5s -> 3.05s, 106x. Data gathering was never the problem: it is ~200ms in both. 99.9% of the endpoint was serialization, which is vf-gff's quadratic StringBuilder in the write direction. No veriframe change made.
close_reason: Root-caused to jolt's quadratic StringBuilder/StringWriter append and fixed there (jolt fix/stringbuilder-quadratic-append, c22ce774). Verified: sbperf 16.1x -> 3.2x scaling, jolt unit clean, corpus 4323/4332 with 0 new divergence, cts 6078 matching baseline, veriframe suite 240 tests/1171 assertions clean under the fixed binary. Run-detail endpoint 322.7s -> 3.2s. No veriframe code change was needed for either.

title: The faithfulness judge failed proofs that prove more than the claim
description:
faithfulness-prompt told the judge to FAIL an artifact expressing something 'stronger, weaker, or simply different'. For the proving direction that is wrong: proving a universal by refuting its negation, an encoding that drops a hypothesis or leaves a sort unconstrained proves a harder theorem, and the claim follows from it.

gen-18 B4 T33 claimed a theorem about a finite set D and encoded D as an unconstrained SMT sort. Z3 returned unsat, proving it for every D. The judge failed it for formalising 'a stronger statement than the claimed finite-set theorem'. That was one of the three consecutive failures that culled B4 — the branch furthest along on Q-A, which had already closed two Lean proofs.

Polarity matters and inverts by direction: for a counterexample the witness must satisfy every hypothesis the claim makes, so generality is not licensed there.
acceptance_criteria: The proving prompt tells the judge a strictly more general formalisation is a PASS and explains that the claim follows from it, while still refusing extra hypotheses or narrowed domains. The refuting and measuring prompts are unchanged in this respect.
close_reason: Fixed, tested, deployed into run 65d50333 over nREPL.

title: An engine outage spent a branch's cull budget
description:
tools/fail set :category :failure on every path, including 'Lean is unavailable' / 'Octave is unavailable' / 'Mathlib search is unavailable'. Those are facts about the process pool, not about the branch.

gen-18 B3 was culled after six consecutive failures while pursuing the reduction of stage 2 to a separable convex cost flow — the strongest line in that run. One of the six was a Lean outage.
acceptance_criteria: An engine that cannot be reached returns a neutral turn and never raises consecutive-failures.
close_reason: Fixed, tested, deployed into run 65d50333 over nREPL.

title: A fork cannot cite a number its parent verified
description:
The done gate's coverage rung reads only (:artifacts branch). Artifacts confirmed elsewhere in the run reach a branch through the shared-artifact block in loop.clj (line 113-125) and the crossover block in beam.clj (line 60-64) — they enter the PROMPT and never the branch's artifact list. So the harness shows a branch evidence and then refuses the answer that cites it.

Concrete casualty this run (0d0c3560): B4.2.2.2 T92 was refused with 'Your answer states figures no artifact supports: 8, 6'. 8 and 6 are the m=3 optimal count and cost, exhaustively verified by Prolog CLPFD on its own parent B4.2.2 and shipped in B4.2.2's accepted answer at T73. The child rewrote its answer to drop them, and in the same edit also dropped its own Lean theorem flowopt_equiv_split (T82, confirmed, all m), so the accepted T94 answer says the explicit-graph link is 'verified at m=1' when the branch had proven it for every m.

This penalises exactly the structure the beam is built on. Every fork inherits its parent's reasoning and none of its evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A branch can cite a claim confirmed by any branch in the same run without the coverage rung refusing it, and the shipped answer attributes it. Regression test: two branches, one banks a numeric artifact, the other's answer states that number and passes.
close_reason: Done gate now reads run-wide confirmed+empirical artifacts, not just the branch's own. Deployed into run 0d0c3560 over nREPL.

title: Only prolog and z3 put the reviewer's objection in the shared failure log
description:
vf-i26 was fixed for verify and verify_smt and left half-done. verify_octave, verify_template, verify_lean and the new measure tool all record a GENERIC reason in the shared failure log: 'the Octave expression does not answer the claim', 'the template's slots do not match the claim'. The objection reaches the branch that made the mistake and dies there.

Observed cost in run 0d0c3560: four separate branches (B2 t5, B4.2.2 t30, B4.3 t29, and B2 t16 in a variant) independently wrote a counter over FEASIBLE flows and claimed it counted L1-OPTIMAL flows, dropping the cost-minimality constraint. The faithfulness judge caught every one and named the fix each time. The failure log — which exists precisely so branches do not repeat each other's dead ends — carried none of it.

Fix: thread the objection into :failure :reason on every path that has one, matching what verify and verify_smt already do.
acceptance_criteria: Every verify_* tool that rejects an artifact as unfaithful records the reviewer's objection, not a generic string, in the shared failure log.
close_reason: Closed

title: A tooling diagnostic can be confirmed, congratulated, and shared to every branch
description:
Live in run 0d0c3560 at turn 4: B3 verified 'Diagnostic: between(-1,1,X) succeeds for X = -1,0,1.', the engine said yes, the harness recorded a CONFIRMED artifact, the milestone gate congratulated it, and with HARNESS_SHARE_ARTIFACTS on it propagated into B1, B2 and B4's context as a shared confirmed result. Nothing about the problem had been established.

This is the exact zebra-run failure advances-thesis? was written for. The guard was inert because B3 had not registered a thesis, and with no thesis the function returns true for any claim — reasonable when the only consumer was the stall counter, wrong now that it is the only relevance signal in the system.

Three consequences, in increasing severity: the stall counter credits it as progress; the milestone and branch-out gates fire on it; and the shared pool exports it to every other branch, which is new with the sharing flag and is how one branch's tooling check becomes four branches' context.

Fix: when no thesis is registered, fall back to the branch's problem statement rather than returning true, and gate entry to the shared pool on the same predicate.
acceptance_criteria: A confirmed claim sharing no substantive vocabulary with the thesis OR the problem does not count as progress, does not fire the milestone or branch-out gates, and does not enter the shared artifact pool.
close_reason: Closed

title: Empirical work cannot be banked, so branches doing it get culled
description:
The phase-unwrap run made 84 octave_eval calls and banked zero artifacts from them. The branch whose thesis was 'empirically locate sigma_MCF' was culled at turn 12 with 0 confirmed artifacts, having done most of that simulation.

The critic scores branches on confirmed artifacts. The only way to bank one is a verify_* call needing a decidable claim, and verify_octave specifically wants one scalar boolean. A sweep that establishes 'recovery breaks around sigma 0.7, and the failure mode is path degeneracy' is the most valuable output available and is not a scalar boolean, so it scores nothing.

Consequence: the beam selects for whatever is easiest to state as a verifiable proposition, which was lemmas about 4-vertex graphs, and against the work that addresses the actual question. 129 of 206 turns went to octave_eval and lean_search that banked nothing.

Two possible fixes: a tool for recording a measurement as evidence (n, parameters, trial count, outcome), or prompt guidance that measurements must be phrased as bankable inequalities on computed counters. The second needs no code.
acceptance_criteria: A branch that measures something real can bank it and score for it.
close_reason: Closed

title: done gate checks evidential support but not relevance to the problem
description:
A branch shipped 'on the 4-cycle with oriented edges e0..e3 ... this refutes the claimed uniqueness lemma' as the final answer to 'when can 2D phase unwrapping be done exactly, and by a polynomial-time algorithm?'. The answer contains no phase field, no noise parameter, no torus, no threshold and no algorithm.

Both gates behaved correctly by their own criteria. The LLM audit passed with 'GAPS: none'. The done gate's uncovered-tokens check verified every substantive token appears in a confirmed artifact — which it does, because the answer IS a confirmed artifact verbatim.

Nothing checks that the answer addresses the problem statement. Same shape as gen-15 shipping a corollary of Balister et al as its final answer.

state.clj already has advances-thesis? for exactly this reason (a run once verified 'clpfd is available' and the milestone gate congratulated it). That guard protects milestones; nothing equivalent guards done.
acceptance_criteria: An answer that does not engage with the problem statement is refused, or the refusal names what it fails to address.
close_reason: Closed

title: An unfaithful prolog artifact was reported to the branch as a success
description:
The prolog verify path set claim-status :unfaithful but left :category :success, :progress? true, and a result string reading 'The goal succeeded with N solution(s)'. The structural objection was journalled and shown to nobody.

Caught live: a branch posted clpfd constraints inside \+ on turn 25, the deterministic check fired, the artifact was marked unfaithful — and the branch was told the goal succeeded, so it repeated the identical defect on turn 26. Two turns burned with no way for the model to learn.

verify_smt, verify_octave and verify_lean all explain an :unfaithful outcome. The prolog path never did; the status was added without the reporting.

Fixed: the structural check is hoisted so its warnings can be quoted back to the branch, an unfaithful outcome now reports :failure with progress? false, and the result carries the objection text plus 'restating the claim to match a goal that enforces nothing is not a fix'.
acceptance_criteria: An unfaithful prolog artifact returns category :failure, scores no progress, and its result names the defect.
close_reason: Fixed and hot-reloaded into the live run over nREPL without restarting it. Test: an-unfaithful-prolog-artifact-is-reported-as-a-failure-with-the-reason.

title: Branch panel hangs forever on any large branch
description:
